title: Superior-to-Michigan-Huron lead correlation exceeded the reverse by 0.038 after three-lag filtering in 1920-2024
abstract: We tested whether Lake Superior monthly changes lead Michigan-Huron changes more strongly than the reverse after each lake season and recent change history were removed. We used coordinated v2025 monthly levels and January 1920 through December 2024 anchors, with forward values through June 2025. After three own-change lags were removed, mean correlation across leads of one to six months was 0.0222 in the flow direction and -0.0162 in reverse. The difference was 0.0384, with a conditional 95% five-year block interval of 0.0040 to 0.0741. Three- and ten-year blocks also gave positive intervals. A twelve-lag filter gave a difference of 0.0322 with an interval of -0.0026 to 0.0669. Separate early and late periods also had intervals that included zero. Thus the primary method found a small directional excess, but its sign was uncertain under a longer filter and shorter periods. Shared weather, regulation and measurement effects remain possible causes. The result does not establish water transport or forecast skill. The package includes code, aggregate evidence, statistic draws, exact source hashes, checks and instructions to regenerate external data outside the publication.

display.caption: Left: residual-change correlations across leads of one to six months after three own-lake lags and month means are removed. Right: mean forward minus reverse correlation with refitted year-block 95% intervals. A longer filter and separate periods leave the sign uncertain. These are statistical relations, not transport or forecast estimates.
